rubric.evidence: Independent source-fidelity review is pending. The leaf review separates the W3C Editor’s Draft, Chrome developer guidance (dated 2025-04-15), ChromeStatus “In development”, and Chromium behavior, but does not establish a conforming cross-implementation contract.

The partial contract now has 22 source-derived items: five headers; four JSON grammar objects; DBSC proof JWT; nine named algorithms; none semantics; federation; and the well-known document. It deliberately no longer treats registration, refresh, lifecycle, or JSON as umbrella inventory buckets.

Every inventory target has visible semantic pre/code HTTP, JSON, or pseudocode examples. Registration and refresh examples now distinguish null-ID no-op termination from removal of an existing refresh session.
Skip link, landmark/heading navigation, semantic table captions and scoped headers, keyboard-focusable overflow-safe code, responsive local navigation, and scroll containers are present.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible long protocol reference navigation responsive tables scrollable HTTP code examples
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use overflow:auto (not forced scroll), stable scrollbar gutters, and contain overscroll so only wide tables/code blocks scroll rather than the document.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied .table-wrap and pre overflow:auto, scrollbar-gutter:stable, overscroll-behavior:contain; mobile table minimum widths remain locally scrollable.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible long-form documentation navigation landmarks skip links
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use landmarks, sequential headings, a skip link with focusable main target, captions and scoped table headers, visible focus, and keyboard-accessible scrollable code.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied skip link to main tabindex=-1, one h1/sequential h2 sections, nav list, table caption/th scope, focus-visible rules, and tabindex=0 on each pre.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible long-form documentation navigation landmarks semantic scrollable code examples
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic pre > code and add tabindex=0 when a pre becomes scrollable; retain native landmarks and document metadata.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All executable protocol examples are semantic pre/code and keyboard focusable; pages retain lang, viewport, title, main and footer.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible external source links in long technical documentation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use semantic links with descriptive accessible names and preserve safe external-link behavior.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The added intent records are visible, descriptive anchors with target=_blank and rel=noopener; they are not represented by unlinked source labels.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible technical documentation semantic tables and code examples
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep technical examples semantic and make data tables navigable with captions and scoped headers.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The source-derived none-semantics addition uses a captioned, scoped table and keyboard-focusable pre/code example; existing reference tables retain the same pattern.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible technical documentation state machine pseudocode examples
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: No directly applicable guidance was returned; preserve semantic pre/code examples and existing document navigation.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The registration/refresh lifecycle distinction is expressed in existing keyboard-focusable semantic pre/code state and pseudocode blocks without adding custom interaction.

openQuestions: The W3C document is an Editor’s Draft and calls itself early. Exact cross-engine shipment, stable Chrome enablement/policy, SSO extensions/attestation parameters, browser key-store behavior, quota values, and retry limits remain unknown or implementation-specific.

Secure-Session-Challenge is unresolved: the Editor’s Draft header section says sf-string; its cache algorithm parses sf-list and requires id for ordinary-response caching; Chromium parses sf-list and accepts a bare member; the Chrome developer guide shows a bare challenge. The reference labels this divergence and does not call any form settled or older.

The current draft says provider_key, provider_session_id, and provider_url are all required for federated key sharing, while Chromium’s current SSO work relaxes provider_session_id validation. The extension is not a settled server contract.

Independent review must establish whether an enabled Chrome population has a portable bare-403 challenge path, and whether that path has a session mapping distinct from the Editor’s Draft ordinary-response cache algorithm.

ChromeStatus’s public Blink intent trail includes Intent to Prototype, Intent to Experiment, and Intent to Ship. Their presence does not settle the current Editor’s Draft grammar, enabled Chrome configuration, or cross-browser availability.

followUpGoals.goal: Obtain independent source-fidelity review resolving the challenge sf-string/sf-list/bare-value divergence and draft/Chromium federation divergence before restoring implementation-sufficient completeness.

summary: Independent review rejected the implementation-sufficient claim. The reference-contract is intentionally partial until review resolves the listed draft, Chrome-guide, and Chromium divergences.
